Ranking: which NASA tests match each habitat's air?
Each PSI combustion investigation is scored against a habitat's O2, pressure and gravity with the fixed rules below. No AI is involved. Weights are our design choice, not a NASA rating.
Moon base: 1 of the 24 PSI combustion investigations ran a test with both O2 and pressure inside this window: PSI-159 (20 tests, gas flames). None used solid materials.
O2

30–100%: "The intermediate oxygen concentration used on the Moon will likely be 30% or greater, with a corresponding pressure of 10.2 psi or less." (Space Apps challenge page) '30% or greater': no upper bound given, so the window runs to 100%.
Pressure
≤ 70.33 kPa (10.2 psi or less): "The intermediate oxygen concentration used on the Moon will likely be 30% or greater, with a corresponding pressure of 10.2 psi or less." (Space Apps challenge page)
Gravity

The headline
It counts solid-material tests only, and only those in our sources (PSI downloads plus 6 cited papers and pages). We do not claim to have seen every test ever run.

The 2 tests inside the Moon-base zone (Saffire VI-2, SIBAL Cloth; Saffire VI-3, Two-Sided PMMA) ran at 20 cm/s airflow, in microgravity. None ran in partial gravity: "there is currently no partial-gravity combustion data available in PSI" (challenge page).

Ranking

Weights (O2 overlap 25, Pressure overlap 20, Flow regime 15, Gravity 15, Material class 15, Test-level data 10) are our design choice, not a NASA rating. Change them and the order changes; the per-component points are shown so you can recompute.
Unknown scores 0. A low score means "the data does not show it", not "it is safe" or "it is dangerous".
Values from summary tables get half credit, because a summary row may list O2 and pressure separately without saying which ran together.

The ISS window comes from two NASA reports (NTRS 20160001047 p.3 and 20150010425 p.1). The rover uses the Moon-base window because the brief gives one atmosphere for both. The spacesuit is scored as used on lunar excursions (partial gravity).
Material class and flow regime are our classification, each tied to a quoted word in the metadata, table or brief (data/manual/investigation_features.csv).

Flame Sandbox

The flame picture is a teaching model, not a simulation. It follows NASA's qualitative description (official challenge video 2:37–3:12; challenge page) and computes nothing: no temperature, size, spread rate or extinction. O2 changes only its brightness; pressure changes nothing in it.
Moon and Mars gravity: no flame is drawn, only the Earth and microgravity outlines, because PSI has no partial-gravity combustion data (challenge page). The sandbox never interpolates between them.
Its evidence panel counts the same 134 solid tests as the Habitat Gaps tab. "Nearby" (±2 points O2, ±5 kPa), flow match (±2 cm/s) and "thin" (≤2) are our display tolerances, not NASA criteria.

The boundary verdict uses BASS-II eq. 6.1 for a 0.318 cm radius PMMA rod only, in microgravity, at 96.53–102.72 kPa and flows 1.01–38.79 cm/s (the recorded stretch rates). Outside that it says "Unknown: no data". The fit is in post-burn O2 while the slider is the cabin O2.

Known Limits
What this site and its sources cannot tell you, so nothing on a chart implies more than the sources say.
The headline
It counts solid-material tests only, and only those in our sources (PSI downloads plus 6 cited papers and pages). We do not claim to have seen every test ever run.

The 2 tests inside the Moon-base zone (Saffire VI-2, SIBAL Cloth; Saffire VI-3, Two-Sided PMMA) ran at 20 cm/s airflow, in microgravity. None ran in partial gravity: "there is currently no partial-gravity combustion data available in PSI" (challenge page).
Two tests are not a flammability boundary. They show that these materials burned under those conditions, not where they stop burning.
Evidence Map, Panel 1 (initial O2 vs pressure)
BASS-II: all 129 PSI-25 rows are plotted at 1 atm (101.325 kPa) because the report states 1 atm; pressure is not logged per test. O2 is the calibrated INITIAL value.

Catalog

The list of 24 investigations is the PSI Combustion Science listing transcribed by hand (data/manual/psi_combustion_index.csv); its count matches the challenge video. PSI-181 (Materials Science) and PSI-108 (Fluid Physics) were in the same listing but are filed under other research areas, so they are left out.
"Test-level data" means a per-test table in our PSI download: 11 yes, 8 summary only, 5 none. PSI raw data (video, sensor logs) runs to terabytes and is not all downloaded.
BASS (PSI-26) has a per-test table but no O2, pressure or flow columns, so it cannot be placed on the Evidence Map.

Metadata quirks are shown as-is, not fixed: Saffire-I and III list the ISS as flight platform though they flew in Cygnus; Saffire I-III share one Hypothesis text; BASS-II assigns no PI role; PSI folder names carry a second number whose meaning we do not know, so it is never used as an ID.
Ranking

Weights (O2 overlap 25, Pressure overlap 20, Flow regime 15, Gravity 15, Material class 15, Test-level data 10) are our design choice, not a NASA rating. Change them and the order changes; the per-component points are shown so you can recompute.
Unknown scores 0. A low score means "the data does not show it", not "it is safe" or "it is dangerous".
Values from summary tables get half credit, because a summary row may list O2 and pressure separately without saying which ran together.

The ISS window comes from two NASA reports (NTRS 20160001047 p.3 and 20150010425 p.1). The rover uses the Moon-base window because the brief gives one atmosphere for both. The spacesuit is scored as used on lunar excursions (partial gravity).
Material class and flow regime are our classification, each tied to a quoted word in the metadata, table or brief (data/manual/investigation_features.csv).

Flame Sandbox

The flame picture is a teaching model, not a simulation. It follows NASA's qualitative description (official challenge video 2:37–3:12; challenge page) and computes nothing: no temperature, size, spread rate or extinction. O2 changes only its brightness; pressure changes nothing in it.
Moon and Mars gravity: no flame is drawn, only the Earth and microgravity outlines, because PSI has no partial-gravity combustion data (challenge page). The sandbox never interpolates between them.
Its evidence panel counts the same 134 solid tests as the Habitat Gaps tab. "Nearby" (±2 points O2, ±5 kPa), flow match (±2 cm/s) and "thin" (≤2) are our display tolerances, not NASA criteria.

The boundary verdict uses BASS-II eq. 6.1 for a 0.318 cm radius PMMA rod only, in microgravity, at 96.53–102.72 kPa and flows 1.01–38.79 cm/s (the recorded stretch rates). Outside that it says "Unknown: no data". The fit is in post-burn O2 while the slider is the cabin O2.
